title: Sephiria Beginner Guide: Side Bag, New Events, First 12 Runs
description: Sephiria beginner guide and walkthrough: first-run priorities, Side Bag rules, Destiny New Events, and combat habits for 1.0.
meta: First 12 runs: Side Bag stays inactive, do Destiny New Events, commit to 1–2 combo tags.
body:
Sephiria throws systems at you fast. Treat the first dozen runs as unlocking the Destiny tree and learning one build sentence—not chasing every shiny Artifact.

The order below is written as three stages: what to settle before the first run, what the first runs are actually for, and what has to be true before you start treating the game as a build game. Every stage has a checkpoint you can check in the client rather than guess at.

Core loop

  • Pick a costume and weapon, enter a floor, choose nodes (Anvil / Dice / combat / shops).
  • Spend Sapphires after runs on the Destiny Inscription permanent tree.
  • Open the Journal (Esc) to review unlocked weapons, Artifacts, Tablets, and Miracles before committing.

First session: settle three choices before the dungeon

A first session is mostly setup, and all three choices are made in the village.

  • Costume. Costumes change opening stats rather than looks, and the starting skins trade one stat against another — defence bought with Max HP, evasion bought with critical chance. Pick the drawback you can live with; the costume roster lists every starting trade, notes which skins have no recorded effect yet, and says what unlocks the rest.
  • Weapon branch. There are six branches and no seventh. Sword and Shield is the branch described as fitting first runs and pattern learning, with short reach as its cost; Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Katana and Staff each carry a different trade. See weapons and upgrades before you commit sapphires to a training node.
  • The one build sentence. Decide which one or two combo families you are chasing this session. Naming them before the floor is what stops a run from collecting five half-sets.

Open the Journal (Esc) once before descending. It is where your save’s unlocks are listed, so the branch and Artifact names in a video are worth less than the list in front of you.

First-run priorities

  • Do New Events on the Destiny tree—they unlock systems (wishing fountain, costumes salon, weapons) that snowball later.
  • Prefer Anvil early so your weapon skill matches the build you are forcing.
  • Side Bag is not free power—items stored there are inactive (including Tablets).
  • Commit to 1–2 combo tags (Storm Cloud, Companion, Glacier, etc.). Diluting five tags starves Tablet payoffs.
Steam Community “Basic Guide” still helps for systems vocabulary, but prefer 1.0-era writeups for route advice after the July 31, 2026 full release.

Side Bag: stored items are inactive

Items in the Side Bag do not contribute their effects, including Tablets. Move the pieces your build needs into the active inventory, then check their adjacency. Use the Side Bag for storage rather than counting it as another active equipment slot. See Artifacts and Tablets for the inventory layout.

What each stage should produce

The checkpoints below are deliberately mechanical. If a row is not true yet, the next stage is where the fix lives; buying further into the tree does not substitute for it.

StageWhat should be trueWhat it unlocks nextWhere to check
Before the first runA costume chosen for its trade-off, one weapon branch chosen, the Journal opened once, one or two combo families namedA floor plan you can actually followCostumes and weapons
First few runsAt least one New Events node bought, one weapon skill line practised at the Anvil, the Side Bag treated as a bench rather than a slotTown systems that pay back every runDestiny Inscription
First boss attemptsThe build holds without depending on a single drop, Tablets sit next to what they buff, inventory is reorganised after bossesFloor 3 pressure, including the library-line fight described on the boss pageYour own inventory board
After Chapter 2The weapon branch is trained, the training ground finished, talents matched to that weaponThe village tree dialogue and later runs of a harder mode — see Hard ModeVillage tree and training ground
Mid-gameOne family is committed, the run can be reassembled without a lucky offer, fountain picks are pre-set for itStage pushes rather than story progress — see Root’s RetreatWishing Fountain and the Journal

What to ignore at the start

  • Tier lists. Published lists disagree with each other and are version-bound; they are useful for picking a branch to learn, not for deciding whether a run worked. Judge by whether your offers complete a route.
  • Costume unlock hunting. Most costumes are unlocked by challenges rather than bought, so the start of the game is a bad time to farm conditions. Play the run you have.
  • A second weapon branch. Training is a sapphire spend plus a training-ground visit; doing it twice before the first build works delays both.
  • Bond Artifact plans. Steam players report that Bond Artifacts are not offered at the fountain, so a build whose whole plan hangs on one is the wrong thing to aim at before the family is stacked.
  • Hard Mode preparation. The mode opens after Chapter 2, and pushing a stage with a half-built run is the mistake the hard-mode page warns about. Nothing about it belongs in session one.
  • Old route advice. Guides written during early access describe systems that have moved; the vocabulary is still useful, the routes are not.

Combat habits that transfer

  • Perfect Guard saves huge MP versus holding block.
  • Reorganize inventory after bosses—adjacency and Tablet geometry matter more than raw rarity.
  • Fruit Skewers bias which combo families appear; frozen fruit can suppress junk families.

Related Sephiria guides

  • Destiny Inscription tree — spend your first sapphires well
  • Sephiria builds — your first real build
  • Hard Mode unlock — what comes after a first clear

The run loop, in four moves

MoveQuestion to answerMistake it prevents
ReadWhat is the nearest threat, what is its attack cue, and where can I retreat?Committing to a long sequence with no exit
CommitWhat is the shortest safe attack sequence that still moves the fight forward?Greeding damage you cannot recover from
CollectWhat does this reward change in the plan I already have?Starting a second unrelated build mid-run
RebuildWhich Artifact and Tablet moves make the next fight easier?Carrying a stale board into a boss

Name the problem before taking the reward

What the run is doingWhat to takeWhat not to take
Enemies survive too longStrengthen a damage source you can actually landA new conditional effect that needs different habits
Mistakes drain healthDefence, recovery, control, a safer rhythmAnother damage tag you cannot keep active
The core already worksUptime and Tablet placement for the existing effectsA fresh unrelated plan
Nothing activates reliablySimplify — keep the clearest triggerMore promises this run cannot fulfil

Source: community beginner walkthrough for 1.0 (sephiria.net), checked 9 November 2026. The framing is theirs; the decision to keep or cut a tag is still yours to make against your own board.

After the run ends

Split the cause into one of five buckets — positioning, an unread attack, weak damage, poor recovery, or an effect that never activated — then change exactly one answer next time. Changing three things at once hides which one worked. Spend the post-run currency on the Destiny tree before chasing another weapon unlock, because the tree is what carries between runs.

What this page does not cover

  • Which upgrade route to finish, and which evolutions exist per branch — see weapons and upgrades.
  • How Artifacts and Tablets fit together, and which Bonds need two tags — see Artifacts and Tablets.
  • Fountain capacity, rarity costs and the talent that expands them — see Wishing Fountain.
  • Where sapphires should go first, and what each node gates — see Destiny Inscription.
  • Fight structure for the first wall and the story climax — see bosses.
  • Hidden rooms and their supplies — see secret rooms.
  • Playing with other people, including the tutorial requirement for every guest — see multiplayer setup and co-op play.

Quick answers for a first session

Do I have to choose a weapon before the first run?

Yes — the core loop starts with a costume and a weapon. The choice is not permanent for the save, but a branch you have not trained limits which Anvil offers turn into a working build, so pick one and practise it.

Why does the Side Bag feel like extra inventory?

Because it holds items without running them. Stored items contribute nothing, Tablets included, so the bag is a bench: move the pieces the build needs into the active inventory and check adjacency there.

Which combo tags should I commit to?

Any one or two of the named families — the page lists Storm Cloud, Companion and Glacier as examples. What matters is the number: one or two, not five, because Tablet payoffs starve when the board is split.

Do Fruit Skewers decide my build?

No. They bias which combo families appear, and frozen fruit can suppress the ones you do not want. They shape the offers; the commitment is still yours.

How long before the game stops feeling random?

The page's own framing is a dozen runs, spent on the Destiny tree and one build sentence. If it still feels random after that, the advice here points at changing too many answers at once rather than at a missing unlock.
